analysis.answer: Current law allows a person 21 or older who lawfully possesses a handgun to carry it concealed without a permit. The measure changes this by requiring a permit from the county sheriff.

There will be administrative costs for county sheriffs to process and issue permits. Individuals seeking to carry concealed handguns will face the opportunity cost of the eight hours required for the safety course, as well as the potential tuition costs for the course.
Handgun owners who wish to carry concealed bear the cost of the time and potential fees for the safety course. Firearms safety instructors benefit from the increased demand for their courses.

Some individuals who currently carry concealed may stop doing so to avoid the time and expense of the safety course and permit process. Others will complete the training, potentially increasing their knowledge of firearm safety. Because the law states the sheriff "shall issue" the permit, sheriffs will process these applications as administrative tasks without discretionary denial for qualified applicants.
Firearms instructors gain a captive market of customers required to take their safety courses. County sheriffs gain an administrative role in processing permits.
